knownLimitations: Coverage is a hand-curated seed list (pipeline/seeds/cases.json), not every election-law case, and not every election case the Court has heard.

The Court's JSON files for the same dockets are not used: its robots.txt asks robots to stay out of the folder they are in.
Docket entries are classified by keyword rules; DemocracyHQ never derives an overall case status.
Filing links are published as the docket gives them and are not individually tested. Only the opinion and order links inside entries are tested on each run.
The absence of a case here says nothing about whether litigation exists.

sources.attribution: U.S. Government Publishing Office, GovInfo: United States Courts Opinions
sources.authority: U.S. Government Publishing Office, from what each court sends it
sources.geographicCoverage: The thirteen federal courts of appeals. District courts and state courts are read from another source, CourtListener.
knownLimitations: Which cases are included is decided by selection rule circuit-select-1, which counts election words and phrases in each opinion and reads the nature of suit in the court's record. It can miss an election case and can pick a case that only mentions elections. Every case a maintainer removed is published with a quoted passage that shows why.

GovInfo holds what each court chooses to send. A court's page here shows how many cases and documents were read for it. For the Eighth Circuit, most of the files are the clerk's cover letter and not the opinion (its page gives the count), so its election cases are found mainly through the nature of suit in the record.

Only opinions and orders a court sends to GovInfo are read. Docket entries, briefs and unsigned orders that a court does not send are not covered, and a pending appeal without an opinion does not appear.

The court a case came from is read from the opinion by a published pattern (origin-court-1). Not every court writes it in a form the pattern reads, so many cases have none; the absence of a district court here does not mean the case did not come from one.
Whether a decision was later reheard, vacated or reviewed by the Supreme Court is not recorded.

sources.attribution: CourtListener, a project of Free Law Project
sources.authority: Free Law Project, a non-profit organisation. It is not a court and not an official source.
sources.geographicCoverage: Federal district courts and the supreme, appellate and trial courts of the states, as far as CourtListener holds their decisions. Its holdings differ much from court to court.
knownLimitations: CourtListener is a collection, not a court. It gathers decisions from the courts' own sites and from other collections, and it does not hold every decision of a court. For many trial courts it holds few decisions or none. A missing case does not mean that nothing was decided.

Which cases are included is decided by selection rule court-select-1: CourtListener's search is asked for decisions with election terms, and the text of each is then counted as for the courts of appeals. It can miss an election case and can pick a case that only mentions elections, or one about an election that is not a public one.

For every other case only decisions are read. A docket, a complaint, a brief or an order that CourtListener does not hold as a decision is not covered, and a pending case without a decision does not appear.

A record is made from CourtListener's copy of a decision and from the case name, docket number, court and date that CourtListener gives. None of it is compared with the court's own record. Where CourtListener recorded the court's own address for a document, the record gives it, unchecked.

Voting cases of the federal district courts are also read from their dockets in the RECAP Archive (rule docket-select-2): the dockets filed since January 1, 2024 to which the clerk gave the nature of suit 441, 'Civil Rights: Voting', whether the docket sheet shows the code or only the words. The archive holds what its users and programs have retrieved from PACER, the courts' paid system. A case nobody has retrieved is missing, a docket may lack its latest entries, and most filings have no copy there. A voting case the clerk filed under another nature of suit is not found.

The entries of such a docket are listed in the clerk's words (rule recap-entry-1). No rule reads them for rulings, so no ruling is named and none of them enters the timeline. The lists of parties and lawyers the archive holds are not read.

A run may send CourtListener a limited number of requests for dockets. A docket that CourtListener has not changed since it was read is not read again; a docket no run has reached yet is missing until a later run reads it.
A court is listed under a state by its name (rule court-state-1). That says where the court sits, not what a case concerns.
Whether a decision was later reheard, vacated, appealed or reviewed is not recorded.

CourtListener limits how often its search may be asked, so the list of decisions is kept month by month and each run may ask the search a limited number of times. The two newest months are asked for first, then the months not read yet, then the months read longest ago; a run normally reads every month. A month the run's requests do not reach is read on the next run. The data and methodology page says how many months have been read and when the one read longest ago was read.
Requires an API token; anonymous requests are refused. Without one the stage does not run and the published cases stay as they are.
sources.license: The decisions of courts are not subject to copyright in the United States. CourtListener's collection and its records are provided by Free Law Project under its terms. The decisions are linked, not mirrored, and every record read from it is labelled 'Imported from secondary source'.
sources.name: CourtListener: decisions of federal district courts and of state courts, and dockets of the RECAP Archive (Free Law Project)

sources.temporalCoverage: Cases with a decision filed, or a docket opened, since January 1, 2024

sources.authority: Plural Policy (non-official aggregator of the legislatures' sites)
sources.geographicCoverage: The legislatures of 49 states and the District of Columbia (California is read from its own data; Puerto Rico is left out)
knownLimitations: Requires an API key, for the list of sessions; the archives themselves need none.

Secondary source: Open States collects the measures from the legislatures' sites, and its records can lag behind them or differ from them. Every record is labelled 'Imported from secondary source' and links to the legislature's own page.

Measures are selected by their titles and by the subjects the legislature files them under (rule state-select-1), never by their text. A measure whose title does not name an election matter, in a legislature that files no subjects, is missed; a title that uses an election word in another sense can be selected.

The stage a measure reached is worked out from the kinds Open States gives its actions (rule state-status-1). It is not the legislature's own status, and an action Open States did not classify does not count.

A measure is listed only where Open States gives an address of the legislature's page that can be opened securely (rule secure-link-1). Where a legislature's pages are given over http only, its measures are listed once its site is found to serve the same pages over https; the list of state legislation names the states this leaves out.
The adapter has read the bulk data since November 2026; the records it writes have not been checked against the official bill pages.
sources.license: Open States data is offered under a public-domain dedication unless otherwise noted; attribution appreciated.
